about: Many datasets are used to evaluate AI methods for intrusion detection, malware and command-and-control analysis, and anomaly detection, but the same dataset name often refers to different releases, captures and derived feature tables.
The Observatory records every dataset at the level of the **release and its distributed artifacts**, and links it to its original publication and distribution source.
eligibility: A dataset is included when it distributes recorded network communications (packet captures, flow records, wireless frames, CAN or V2X messages, protocol logs) or features demonstrably derived from them, whatever the security task. Host-only telemetry, malware binaries and sensor time series without a network-traffic component are not eligible on their own.

model_intro: Each dataset of the Observatory is described by the same entity model as the paper: the dataset at the centre, linked to ten entities. The five above it describe where the dataset comes from (dashed lines are optional associations: not every dataset has a family, a paper or a derivation tool); the five below describe what it contains and how to get it. Every value is also a filter of the catalogue: select one to see the datasets that have it.

top.name: Family
top.text: The named line of related collections the dataset belongs to, e.g. the Stratosphere Malware Capture Facility. Datasets of one family share sources and are not independent.

top.name: Paper
top.text: The publications that introduce or use the dataset; each card links the original one.

top.name: Lineage
top.text: Whether the dataset is a new acquisition or is derived from another dataset (a re-extraction, a subset, a merge). A derived dataset links its parents, and a parent shows its derived datasets.

top.name: Labeling
top.text: How traffic is labelled: one benign/attack label, one label per attack class, or labels inferred from heuristics such as IDS alerts or file names.

top.name: Derivation Tool
top.text: The tool that produced the derived artifacts from the traces, when there are any (e.g. CICFlowMeter, Zeek, Argus, nfdump).

bottom.name: Domain
bottom.text: The application domain: one of the paper tables, which also gives the colour of the card.

bottom.name: Capture Scenario
bottom.text: Where the traffic was captured: on real devices and networks, in a simulator or emulator, or in a testbed that mixes the two.

bottom.name: Attack Families
bottom.text: The kinds of attack the dataset covers, grouped in common families across the tables.

bottom.name: Artifact
bottom.text: What is actually delivered to researchers: the network traces themselves (packets, CAN or V2X messages) and/or information derived from them (flows, feature tables).

bottom.name: Access Route
bottom.text: How the artifacts are obtained: a direct download, a download after registration, or a request to the authors.
